title: Project Connect slice 1 — governed remote participation (candidate)

remote_session_policy.$comment: certification requires the pause policy within 2 × bound (R-FED-21a); asserted by PC-DISC-4

exclusions.what: R-CORE-34(a) key storage outside the database
R-OPS-11 build identity changes with deployed code

exclusions.why: D10: HTTP on loopback; transport not proven

pc-ref.$comment: not 4190: that port is on the Fetch standard blocked-ports list (sieve)

actors.$comment: Actor and credential table (CDX-06). Credentials are provisioned at startup by each node's admin, outside the black-box run, and never appear in evidence.
actors.synthetic_human: Homed on the scenario's home node. On Beta: created through the SCR-1 synthetic-principal provisioning credential. On pc-ref: created through the runner's own node.
actors.claim_minting: POST /ilp/v1/claims on the home node, authenticated by the SCR-1 provisioning credential with on_behalf_of = the synthetic human.
actors.operator_credential: ilpo_ scoped conformance-operator credential: one test event on the host; approve/reject joins, revoke grants and tokens; revocable, audited.
actors.peering_credential: ilpf_ peering-scoped credential: add, suspend, reinstate, remove peers.
actors.provisioning_credential: ilpp_ SCR-1 credential: create principals marked synthetic, mint claims for them, revoke them. Never usable on non-synthetic principals.
actors.events: Created per scenario and repetition by the host's admin at startup: E1 (federated, live, remote allowed), E2 (same policy), E-short (grant_ttl_s = short_grant_ttl_s), E-mandate (mandates_allowed = [human_directed, human_approved]), E-excl (grant actions [proposal, vote], exclusions [vote]), E-private (private control), E-local (non-federated control with a local participant). Federation policy is set through federation_policy before the run.
actors.non_synthetic_principal: The host admin's own human global ID, given to the runner so PC-PROV-1 can attempt forbidden operations on it.
actors.negative_claim_signer: pc-aux — a second runner-owned reference node, peered with every node under test. The runner signs negative claims (NF-4, NF-6) with pc-aux's own key; no key of any node under test is ever used (R-CONF-1).
actors.outage_control: PC-REV-4 and PC-REV-5 stop and restart the home node through the local harness (declared ops drill; the host under test is never touched).

interfaces.federation_policy: POST /ilp/v1/events/{event}/federation-policy {grant_ttl_s, mandates_allowed, grant_actions, grant_exclusions} [admin, setup only]
interfaces.claims: POST /ilp/v1/claims {purpose, event, aud, agent, on_behalf_of, consent_accepted} [provisioning credential]
interfaces.actions: POST /ilp/v1/events/{event}/actions {kind, payload, mandate} [Bearer ilpt_; optional ILP-Grant header (SCR-2); Idempotency-Key]
interfaces.revocations: GET /ilp/v1/federation/revocations?since=<seq> (public in 0.0.2; each record is signed)

no_side_effect_observables: action count (feed records of kind action)

evidence_packet.content_manifest: content.json — format pc-evidence/1: profile id + sha256, spec version, subjects (build, deployment, discovery hash, keys), runner, files[], summary
evidence_packet.attestations: ilp-attestation+jwt per node and per runner over content_root

tests.title: Discovery document is served at /.well-known/interlateral.json and validates against the strict discovery schema

Build identity is present and stable: instance.software.build and instance.deployment_id are non-empty, equal across fetches, and equal to the values bound into the evidence packet. (That the build changes when code changes is verify: review, R-OPS-11.)
tests.expect: two fetches equal; non-empty build and deployment_id

tests.title: spec_versions declares the profile's specification version; protocols includes ilp/1; instance.host has no scheme, port, or path

Keys: every key is an Ed25519 OKP JWK; federation.active_kid names a listed key; every signed object observed in the run carries the active kid; revocation_bound_s ≤ profile bound; the declared remote_session_policy is pause with after_s ≤ parameters.remote_session_policy.after_s_max
tests.expect: active kid used by claims, grants, revocations

tests.title: Key custody ops drill: started in production mode with its key file absent, the node refuses to start; started in declared development mode with a key file present, the node does not replace it
Problem documents: type = urn:ilp:error:<CODE>, title = <CODE>, status = HTTP status, served as application/problem+json
tests.expect: every negative response in the run conforms

tests.title: Lenient receive: a claim carrying an unknown x_ member (signed) is accepted; a claim carrying a non-x_ unknown member is accepted and the member ignored
JWS discipline: a claim with alg none, or alg other than EdDSA, is rejected with SIGNATURE_INVALID; a claim whose kid does not resolve is rejected with UNKNOWN_SIGNER
Error precedence: an out-of-scope action attempted in a phase that forbids it reports GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION, not PHASE_MISMATCH
Receipt wire form: served receipts use member `resource` (never resource_global_id), validate against the receipt schema, and the chain recomputes from sixty-four zeros
tests.expect: chain verifies with the reference library

tests.title: Explicit mutual peering: each admin (or peering credential) adds the other; both peer lists show the other as active with common_spec_versions non-empty
A join request whose claim is issued by a non-peer is rejected with NOT_A_PEER, with no shadow principal created

Peering state changes (suspend, reinstate) are visible on the public peer list (a suspended peer is listed as suspended) and are published as signed revocation records of kind peer; the reinstatement record carries reinstated: true; a removed peer disappears from the public list and can be re-added. (The proposed state is not reachable through the declared interfaces in 0.0.2: an admin's peering act is its approval.)
The host lists its federated event; every entry validates against directory-entry and carries the event's global ID, pack, status, policy, and home
A private control event and a non-federated control event never appear in the directory, locally or aggregated
The home aggregates its active peer's directory: the host's event appears with the same global ID and is labeled with its home host
tests.expect: aggregated entry equal on identifying members

tests.title: updated_at is monotonic per entry, and a closed event is reported with status closed

The home mints an ilp-claim+jwt: typ, EdDSA, active kid; payload valid against identity-claim; sub = the on_behalf_of synthetic human; aud = host; exp − iat ≤ 86400; no email or out-of-schema member; a claim request whose aud is not an active peer is refused with NOT_A_PEER
tests.expect: valid claim; NOT_A_PEER for a non-peer aud

tests.title: The host accepts a valid claim (202 pending, retrieval key) and creates a remote shadow principal keyed by the home global ID; identity alone confers nothing: an action authenticated only by the claim returns AUTHZ_REQUIRED

Claim validation: a replayed claim is rejected with CLAIM_REPLAYED; a claim for another audience with CLAIM_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH; an expired claim with CLAIM_EXPIRED; a tampered claim with SIGNATURE_INVALID

After approval, the authenticated join retrieval delivers the participant token and an ilp-grant+jwt: typ, EdDSA, active kid; payload valid; iss = aud = host; sub = home global ID; agent bound; authorization_details names unconference@1.1 unconference.proposal; exp − iat ≤ test-grant TTL; credential_binding = S256(token)
tests.expect: valid grant bound to the delivered token

tests.title: Grant status is public and secret-free (active), and the bearer can re-fetch the same grant at /ilp/v1/auth/grant
A grant used after exp (plus skew) is rejected with GRANT_EXPIRED and status reports expired

The permitted act's receipt carries authorization_grant = grant jti, subject_human = home global ID, subject_agent = home agent global ID, license_plate, mandate, source_class agent_token_api; the hash recomputes and links
Idempotency: a retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original result and creates no second action, feed record, or receipt
Join approval and grant issuance each produce a receipt and feed records on the host
The permitted action (unconference.proposal) by the remote agent is accepted exactly once, under the grant
The out-of-scope action (unconference.vote) is rejected with GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION and produces no action, feed record, receipt, or tally change
A token and grant issued for event E1 used against event E2 on the same host is rejected with GRANT_EVENT_MISMATCH, with no side effects
A presented grant issued by another host is rejected with GRANT_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH, with no side effects
A presented grant with an altered payload byte is rejected with SIGNATURE_INVALID, with no side effects
A presented grant bound to another participant's token is rejected with GRANT_BINDING_MISMATCH, with no side effects
An expired grant authorizes nothing: the act is rejected with GRANT_EXPIRED and no side effects

A grant revoked by the host operator is rejected on next use with GRANT_REVOKED (or AUTH_REVOKED when the token is revoked with it), its status is revoked, and a signed revocation record of kind grant is published

On the E-mandate event, the delivered grant carries mandates_allowed = [human_directed, human_approved] (asserted first); an act declaring standing_instruction is rejected with GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION + code_detail MANDATE_NOT_ALLOWED and no side effects
A grant is not a bearer credential: Authorization: Bearer <grant JWS> is rejected with AUTH_INVALID, and ILP-Grant with no Authorization is rejected with AUTH_MISSING, both with no side effects

Narrowing only: (a) on the E-excl event, whose grant lists unconference.vote in both authorization_details and exclusions, a vote is rejected with GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION; (b) a grant-permitted proposal beyond the engine's per-participant cap is rejected (VOTE_CAP_EXCEEDED or CONFLICT); both with no side effects
The revocation feed serves signed ilp-revocation+jwt records, valid against revocation-record, with strictly increasing seq and the {items, next_cursor, latest_seq} envelope
The home revokes the participant's agent; within revocation_bound_s the host rejects the next act (AUTH_REVOKED or GRANT_REVOKED) and a new join by that subject is rejected with SUBJECT_REVOKED

The host suspends the home peer: the remote participant's next act and a new join are rejected with PEER_SUSPENDED and the grant status reads suspended; after reinstatement the ORIGINAL token and grant act again (status active) — suspension is resumable

Fail closed: when the home's revocation feed cannot be refreshed for 2 × bound, a new join from that peer is rejected with REVOCATION_STATE_UNKNOWN (503, retry_after), and an already-admitted remote participant is handled per the declared remote_session_policy (pause → REVOCATION_STATE_UNKNOWN); after the home returns and a refresh succeeds, that participant acts again
Outage isolation: while the home is unreachable, the host's local event accepts a local participant's act

The ilpp_ provisioning credential cannot mint a claim for, or revoke, a non-synthetic principal (FORBIDDEN), and cannot add peers, moderate joins, revoke grants, or act in an event (rejected: FORBIDDEN or AUTH_INVALID); no state changes
Golden thread with Beta-A as home and Beta-B as host passes end to end (PEER-1, IDC-1..3, GRANT-1..2, ENF-1..2, RCPT-1)
Golden thread with Beta-B as home and Beta-A as host passes end to end
The host's ilp-export/1 bundle validates, is signed by the active kid, and additively includes grants.jsonl, revocations.jsonl, and claims.jsonl (consent-filtered, no email)
pc-verify accepts the complete packet offline with network denied, and rejects each negative packet for the stated reason
